title: A11y-first neutral palette and contextual elevation matrix
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Our neutral palette and elevation rules have drifted across components. Several teams have created ad‑hoc gray ramps and shadow presets which causes inconsistent perceived contrast, especially in low‑contrast and high‑density surfaces (tables, embedded widgets). This increases accessibility regressions and forces engineering to add per-component overrides.

Goal: Rework the neutral color system and elevation matrix to be accessibility‑first, deterministic, and context‑aware. Deliver a single neutral ramp with explicit contrast anchors for text and UI elements, a contextual elevation matrix that composes penumbra + ambient layers, and a spacing/radius guidance that scales with density. The tokens must be implementable as variables (CSS custom properties / token JSON), with usage examples for buttons, tables, charts, and card surfaces.

Scope:
- Canonical neutral palette (Lab-based derivation) with named anchors for accessibility: neutral-00..neutral-100, and semantic aliases (bg, surface, muted, subtle).
- Contrast anchors flagged for AA and AAA text sizes and UI elements (labels, placeholders, disabled states).
- Contextual elevation matrix: three composable layers (penumbra, umbra, ambient) that can be toggled per density or component context.
- Radius scale with two axes: component-radius (buttons/inputs) and container-radius (cards/panels) plus a micro-radius for dense tables.
- Update typography scale tokens to explicit pixel and relative values and map which sizes are required to meet AA/AAA with the neutral anchors.
- Documentation, Figma tokens, and a GH PR with token JSON + examples.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical neutral ramp defined in tokens JSON and published to tokens-2026.03 namespace
Contrast anchors documented: examples showing which token pairs meet AA/AAA for body, caption, small UI text
Elevation matrix implemented as three composable token layers and demonstrated on Card/Button/Table components in Figma
Radius scale added to token JSON with migration notes for button and table components
Documentation page in Confluence with rationale, math for Lab derivation, and rollout checklist
Design review sign-off from Accessibility (A11y) and Product Design leads
Engineering PR with unit examples and Storybook fixtures merged or linked to rollout plan
tasks: Derive neutral ramp from base Lab anchors and create token variants for light/dark modes
Calculate contrast ratios for all neutral anchors against primary text sizes
Design elevation layer recipes (penumbra, umbra, ambient) and create parameterized tokens
Rebaseline typography scale and produce mapping doc: token -> px/rem -> recommended usage
Produce Figma file with component variants (button, card, table) using new tokens
Write tokens JSON and add to repo under tokens-2026.03 namespace
Run accessibility evals against representative pages (dashboard, table-list, embed)
design_decisions: Use Lab color space to derive neutral ramp to preserve perceptual steps across light/dark
Expose explicit contrast anchors (neutral-10, neutral-30, neutral-70) rather than allowing arbitrary grays
Elevation is represented as three composable layers to allow deterministic stacking and simpler interpolation for density scaling
Radius will be two-axis: component-radius and container-radius to better handle micro vs macro geometry
Typography scale will default to variable font metrics where available, with pixel fallbacks to ensure consistent contrast calculations
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Migration will break in-product components that rely on legacy gray stops. Mitigation: Provide a migration script and a compatibility alias section in tokens JSON.
Risk: Engineering adoption lag. Mitigation: Provide Storybook examples and a small SDK helper (css variables + Sass mixins) to make swapping trivial.
Risk: Visual regressions in high-density tables. Mitigation: Create density test fixtures and run visual diffs before rollout.
